newsitem.title: USA: Reno likely to remain in Cabinet, officials say.
newsitem.headline: Reno likely to remain in Cabinet, officials say.

text.p: President Bill Clinton will keep Attorney General Janet Reno in his Cabinet if Reno, who is ill with Parkinson's disease, wants to stay on, top administration officials said on Thursday.

Clinton himself passed up a chance to end speculation about Reno's future when asked about it at a White House photo session, saying that she was among "four or five of my Cabinet members that I haven't met with."
"I'm going to try to get it all done by the end of the week," he told reporters.

But a source familiar with the president's thinking said he would be "very surprised" if Clinton did not ask Reno to remain in the Cabinet. "If she wants to stay, I'm sure she can," another official said.

Questions about Reno's job security have arisen because of her independent streak, which has often irked the White House. Some Clinton aides have also complained that she has been too quick to bow to partisan calls for independent counsel probes.
Reno, who has repeatedly -- and publicly -- said she would like to continue in her present job, was cautious at a news conference on Thursday when asked if she would remain at the Justice Department.
"Anything like that the president has to talk about," she said. Asked if the time had come for a decision on her future, Reno replied: "You would have to ask them."

Reno, 58, a blunt-talking former Florida prosecutor who was Clinton's third choice for the nation's top law enforcement post initially, was diagnosed with Parkinson's disease a year ago and sometimes shows a slight trembling that is one of the symptoms of the disease.
But Justice Department officials said she is in the early stage of that illness, and is physically capable of continuing to carry out her present duties.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Clinton had spoken to Reno by telephone on the eve of her maiden argument before the U.S. Supreme Court on Wednesday, and that they had a good conversation. He said they would meet Thursday or Friday.
